title: Cap. 6 Arg. 7 close: After Christ, who has applying grace turns on divine good pleasure, not human disparity
pass_a_gloss: Therefore after Christ has been given to us, this distinction—that some have that grace by which they apply Christ to themselves unto salvation, others do not have it—is reduced not to the disparity of human wills, but to the good pleasure of the divine will.
pass_b_english: So after Christ has been given us, the distinction that some have the grace by which they apply Christ to themselves for salvation, and others do not, is brought back not to the unevenness of human wills, but to the good pleasure of the divine will.
source_text: Ergo post datum nobis Christum, non ad disparitatem humanarum voluntatum, sed ad beneplacitum Divinae voluntatis reducitur hoc discrimen, quod aliqui habeant eam gratiam qua Christum sibi applicant ad salutem, alii non habeant.
